extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit communications staff, PR/marketing professionals, and NGO press officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for writing press releases for nonprofits/NGOs that raise awareness, attract donors/volunteers, and communicate impact while protecting beneficiaries and aligning with mission. Covers headline, lead, body, quotes, event releases, privacy, donor recognition, and an implicit quality checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary aims a nonprofit press release should achieve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get people talking about philanthropic initiatives; generate publicity for fundraising, disaster management, aid; raise awareness about mission and programs; attract donors and volunteers; build credibility within community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for the press release headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 100 characters; grab attention while showing impact; focus on difference made (not just news); use active voice; show stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: What the opening paragraph must communicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the five Ws (who, what, when, where, why); explain WHY the reader should care; connect to mission; put beneficiaries front and center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body
rubrics_metrics.description: Core content to include in the body of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly communicate goals; explain why the story is newsworthy; include direct quotes from experts; provide statistics on impact; share success stories; include beneficiary testimonials (with consent); supply program details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on whose voices to include and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quotes from executive director/founder, beneficiaries (with consent), program partners, and major donors where appropriate to add authority, humanize the story, and demonstrate impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Topics for Nonprofit Releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical subjects that merit a nonprofit press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant funding received; awards received; new executive hire; major donor announcement; rebranding; program launches; annual reports; fundraising events; partnership announcements; crisis response activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charity Event Releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific requirements when the release is announcing or promoting an event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drive attendance and donations; create buzz; explain why the event matters; include specific date, time, location; state cost and registration info; list notable attendees/speakers; describe direct beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and ethical guidance for handling beneficiary information and media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain consent for stories and photos; use first names only when needed; anonymize when appropriate; avoid exploitation; show dignity and agency of beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor Recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle naming and acknowledging donors in releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name major donors only with permission; communicate levels of giving; respect anonymous donors; promote match challenges when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission Connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to tie each release back to organizational mission and goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every release should tie to mission; include statistics on the cause; reference long-term goals; cite impact metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission-aligned
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative criterion: release aligns with organizational mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the release clearly connects news to the nonprofit's stated mission and strategic priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary-focused (not org-focused)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative criterion: emphasis on beneficiaries instead of self-promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrative should foreground beneficiary needs, outcomes, and dignity rather than org-centric praise or promotional language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific impact (numbers, stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative criterion: provides concrete evidence of impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include measurable impact (statistics, metrics) and illustrative personal stories to substantiate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor recognition appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative criterion: donor acknowledgement handled sensitively and correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm permission before naming donors; represent levels and recognition properly; respect anonymity requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary consent obtained
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative and ethical criterion: consent for use of beneficiary stories and images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and verify consent for testimonials and photos; anonymize when consent is not granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program partner attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative criterion: partners and collaborators are credited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute program partners clearly and accurately to show collaboration and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding sources transparent
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative criterion: transparency about who funds the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose major funding sources where relevant to avoid perception of hidden influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer/donor call-to-action
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative criterion: includes clear ways readers can help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific, actionable calls-to-action for volunteers and donors (how to give, register, volunteer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax ID / 501(c)(3) noted
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative disclosure criterion often expected in nonprofit releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include tax ID or 501(c)(3) designation when appropriate to facilitate donations and establish nonprofit status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reports linked
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion: provide links to organizational reporting for transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to annual reports or financials to support claims and allow deeper scrutiny by donors and press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia (beneficiaries with consent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guideline to enhance coverage with multimedia assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include photos, video, or other multimedia of beneficiaries only with documented consent; use multimedia to illustrate impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive language
rubrics_metrics.description: Style guideline to avoid exclusionary or stigmatizing wording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use inclusive, respectful language that centers dignity and avoids stereotypes or stigmatizing descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoids savior narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical/content guideline to prevent patronizing framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame beneficiaries as agents; avoid language that depicts the organization as rescuing helpless people or communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest about challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle of candidness about limitations and difficulties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about ongoing challenges and complexities rather than overstating success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides ways to help
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical requirement to include concrete engagement options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always provide clear, specific instructions on how readers can help (donate link, volunteer sign-up, contacts, registration).
